notes:
Summary: OrbitalSmith is a developer tools startup building an IDE copilot (in-editor streaming completions + completions-as-you-type). They operate a nightly indexing/embedding refresh (approx 2M source files, mixture of repos and generated docs). Primary evaluation: whether Redwood can provide sub-200ms p95 streaming for small completions (3-6 tokens), predictable cost for embedding refresh, and easy model pinning for staged rollouts.

Key technical requirements:
- Low-latency streaming: IDE plugin requires token streaming with p95 < 200ms and tail controls. CTO quote: "We can't have 500ms hiccups in the editor — devs feel it immediately."
- Embeddings refresh: Batch-optimized pipeline that can re-embed entire codebase nightly; current throughput target ~6000 req/s during peak window; interested in larger batch sizes (128-512) and prefix/KV cache reuse to reduce token cost.
- Model/version pinning: Need canary rollouts for new model versions and automatic fallback to quantized variants when dedicated capacity is saturated.
- Security/compliance: SSO/SAML, SOC2 evidence required, audit logs, KMS for key material, and EU data residency for subset of customers.

POC scope: 2-week run where Redwood will: deploy a dedicated pool (or hosted test config), run a scaled-down embedding refresh (500k files) with batching profiles suggested by Optimize, instrument token-level cost, and validate streaming latency with developer instrumentation. Success metrics: embedding cost < $0.02/doc average (target), streaming p95 < 200ms, model pinning + rollback demo.

Stated constraints/blockers: legal needs SOC2 appendix; infra needs VPC peering detail for nightly bulk transfers; ops wants clear autoscaling behavior during embedding spikes.

Misc: referenced artifacts — pricing deck (drive link), security FAQ (drive link), Fireflies call ff-20260301-48ab (demo transcript), Jira INF-1327 for POC infra. AE notes: keep communications concise, provide a pre-filled security questionnaire, and propose a short canary plan for model rollouts.
